description: the corner of elm street where the sidewalk buckles and a narrow alley mouth opens between two darkened storefronts. a dead streetlight hums overhead, its bulb long gone. the taco bell's buzzing sign is the brightest thing for a block, spilling green-white light across the cracked pavement. an old bus stop bench leans against the wall, peeling to the wood, and someone has scratched a lopsided heart and a run-on apology into the grime on the glass of the adjacent storefront. it's the kind of corner you round without thinking — and the kind where, on a bad night, you walk straight into someone coming the other way.

environment.noise: distant traffic, the taco bell sign buzzing
environment.smell: old brick, wet asphalt, cold dumpster

items.name: Bus Stop Bench
items.description: a wooden bench bolted to the pavement, paint flaking to pale grey. a faded ad panel above it has been scraped to nothing. someone left a crushed green monster can wedged under one leg.

items.name: Graffiti Wall
items.description: the dark storefront window beside the alley mouth, grimy enough to write in. a half-hearted heart with an arrow, and below it, in smaller letters, 'sorry — i mean it this time'.

name: Sidewalk Corner

exits.description: the sidewalk continues along elm street, buckled in patches, the taco bell's buzzing sign pulling the eye a few doors down.
